newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOUTH AFRICA EXPORTS RAGGED-TOOTH SHARKS.
newsitem.headline: SOUTH AFRICA EXPORTS RAGGED-TOOTH SHARKS.

text.p: South African zoologists said on Tuesday they were doing a brisk business catching ragged-tooth sharks and exporting them to European aquariums.
Cape Town zoologist John Visser said the sharks, common along the southern coast near the town of East London, were popular overseas.
He has caught six sharks, the largest a metre (yard) long and hopes to send six each of six different species to Dutch, Portuguese and other foreign aquariums.
The captured sharks are being stored at a tidal pool and in East London aquarium.
Visser has previously exported sharks to Hong Kong, the United States, the Netherlands, Germany and Portugal.
He said: "The ragged tooth shark breeds extremely well in captivity."
Visser was reluctant to say how much the sharks cost to capture and export, and how much they were sold for.
